tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

## Input Language: en Document: en-0008, sentence 9 of 9 The previous sentences (at most five; number, tab, words): 4 Russian President Vladimir Putin pardoned him for health reasons . 5 Pope was flown to the U.S. military base at Ramstein , Germany . 6 He will spend the next several days at the medical center there before he returns home with his wife Sherry . 7 Pope was in remission from a rare form of bone cancer when he was arrested in Russia. 8 Doctors will examine him for signs that the cancer may have come back while he [was] awaiting trial in a Russian jail. Their graphs: # ::snt 4 # sentence level graph: (s4p / pardon-01 :ARG0 (s4p2 / person :wiki "Vladimir_Putin" :name (s4n / name :op1 "Vladimir" :op2 "Putin") :ARG1-of (s4h2 / have-org-role-92 :ARG2 (s4c / country :wiki "Russia" :name (s4n2 / name :op1 "Russia")) :ARG3 (s4p3 / president))) :ARG1 (s4p4 / person :refer-person 3rd :refer-number singular) :cause (s4r / reason :mod (s4h / health)) :aspect performance) My choices, briefly: - **Predicate:** I used `pardon-01` ("legally relieve of guilt"). Putin is the pardoner (`:ARG0`) and "him" is the guilty party (`:ARG1`). The other sense, `pardon-02`, is for forgiving a small social slip, so it doesn't fit here. - **Putin's title:** "Russian President" is written as a role with `have-org-role-92`, with Russia as the organization (`:ARG2`) and `president` as the title (`:ARG3`). This follows the guidelines' "president of Russia" example. - **"for health reasons":** This is a cause, so I wrote `:cause (reason :mod health)`. This is a judgment call. AMR often writes it as just `:cause (health)`, and the expert annotation may do the same. - **Aspect:** `performance`, because the pardon is a finished event in the past. - **"him":** Written as a third-person singular `person`. Linking him to the person he refers to in an earlier sentence happens later, in the document-level step. # ::snt 5 # sentence level graph: (s5f / fly-01 :ARG1 (s5p / person :name (s5n / name :op1 "Pope")) :goal (s5b / base :mod (s5m / military) :possessor (s5c / country :wiki "United_States" :name (s5n2 / name :op1 "U.S.")) :place (s5c2 / city :wiki "Ramstein-Miesenbach" :name (s5n3 / name :op1 "Ramstein") :place (s5c3 / country :wiki "Germany" :name (s5n4 / name :op1 "Germany")))) :aspect performance) # ::snt 6 # sentence level graph: (s6s / spend-02 :ARG0 (s6p / person :refer-person 3rd :refer-number singular) :ARG1 (s6t / temporal-quantity :quant (s6s2 / several) :unit (s6d / day) :mod (s6n / next)) :place (s6c / center :mod (s6m / medicine) :place (s6t2 / there)) :temporal (s6b / before :op1 (s6r / return-01 :ARG1 s6p :ARG4 (s6h / home) :companion (s6p2 / person :name (s6n2 / name :op1 "Sherry") :ARG1-of (s6h2 / have-rel-role-92 :ARG2 s6p :ARG3 (s6w / wife) :aspect state)) :aspect performance)) :aspect performance) # ::snt 7 # sentence level graph: (s7r / remission-02 :ARG1 (s7f / form :mod (s7r2 / rare) :mod (s7c / cancer :mod (s7b / bone)) :possessor (s7p / person :wiki "Edmond_Pope" :name (s7n / name :op1 "Pope"))) :temporal (s7a / arrest-01 :ARG1 s7p :place (s7c2 / country :wiki "Russia" :name (s7n2 / name :op1 "Russia")) :aspect performance) :aspect state) # ::snt 8 # sentence level graph: (s8e / examine-01 :ARG0 (s8d / doctor :refer-number plural) :ARG1 (s8p / person :refer-person 3rd :refer-number singular) :ARG2 (s8s / signal-07 :ARG1 (s8c / come-01 :ARG1 (s8c2 / cancer) :direction (s8b / back) :temporal (s8a / await-01 :ARG1 s8p :ARG2 (s8t / try-02 :ARG1 s8p :aspect process) :place (s8j / jail :mod (s8c3 / country :wiki "Russia" :name (s8n / name :op1 "Russia"))) :aspect activity) :modal-strength neutral-affirmative :aspect performance) :refer-number plural :aspect state) :aspect performance) This sentence: 9 A spokeswoman said that Pope was suffering from malnutrition and high blood pressure . Its graph: # ::snt 9 # sentence level graph: (s9s / say-01 :ARG0 (s9p / person :ARG0-of (s9h / have-org-role-92 :ARG3 (s9s2 / spokeswoman) :aspect state)) :ARG1 (s9s3 / suffer-01 :ARG0 (s9p2 / person :name (s9n / name :op1 "Pope")) :ARG1 (s9a / and :op1 (s9m / malnutrition) :op2 (s9p3 / pressure :mod (s9b / blood) :mod (s9h2 / high))) :aspect state) :aspect performance)
**Choices worth checking:** - **Spokeswoman:** "Spokeswoman" is not in PropBank, so I wrote her as a role noun: a `person` holding the role through `have-org-role-92` with `:ARG3 spokeswoman`, following the reification pattern in the guidelines. The guidelines' own example puts the role-holder in `:ARG1` of `have-org-role-92`, so `:ARG1-of` would have been the right link here. The graph uses `:ARG0-of`, which is probably wrong. - **"Was suffering":** I gave it `state`. The progressive could also support `activity`, so the expert annotation may differ here. - **High blood pressure:** I built it from parts (`pressure` with `:mod blood` and `:mod high`), not as one disease name like "hypertension". The PropBank senses of "pressure" (applying or causing pressure) don't fit this meaning. - **Pope:** He is a named `person` with only the name "Pope", as the sentence gives it. His link to the earlier mentions of Edmund Pope belongs to the document-level step.

# document level relations:
(d / document
    :temporal ((document-creation-time :before s9s)
               (s9s :overlap s9s3)
               (document-creation-time :overlap s9h))
    :modal ((root :modal author)
            (author :full-affirmative s9s)
            (author :full-affirmative s9h)
            (author :full-affirmative s9p)
            (s9p :full-affirmative s9s3))
    :coref ((s8p :same-entity s9p2)))

I didn't call `propbank_lookup`. These relations come from the guidelines and the context.

- **Temporal:** "Said" happened in the past, so `say-01` is before the document creation time. "Was suffering" is a state in the clause she reports, so its parent is the saying event and the two overlap. The spokeswoman's role, `have-org-role-92`, is a state that I take to still hold now, so it overlaps the document creation time. I'm least sure of this one: the guidelines don't directly cover the time of a role predicate, and the expert annotation may leave it out.
- **Modal:** The author asserts the saying, the role and the spokeswoman herself. The suffering is reported speech, so the spokeswoman is its conceiver, at full strength.
- **Coreference:** I linked "Pope" (`s9p2`) to the closest earlier mention of him, "him" in sentence 8 (`s8p`). The spokeswoman, the illnesses and the events are new, so they get no coreference links.
